meta.description: Turns untargeted LC-MS/MS features (m/z, RT, MS/MS) into confidence-stratified metabolite annotations using spectral-library matching (matchms), in-silico tools (SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID, MetFrag) and molecular networking, and assigns a defensible MSI/Schymanski confidence level.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 13 cited references unchanged from the pre-fix Skill (Sumner 2007, Schymanski 2014, Li 2021, Duhrkop 2019/2021, Hoffmann 2022, Ruttkies 2016, Wang 2016, Nothias 2020, Kind & Fiehn 2006, Zhou 2020, Theodoridis 2023, Huber 2020) remain real, verifiable, and cited accurately; no fabricated statistics or invented values appeared in any of the 7 executed outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Chemical/analytical annotation only; no output makes a diagnostic, prescriptive, or individual-patient claim.

methodological_ground.detail: No output substitutes correlation for causation or overclaims identity; the fixed Skill still actively warns against treating a cosine score as identity and now demonstrably enforces the isomer-wall warning in its own executable code (Inputs 3, 5, 6), not just prose.

code_usability.detail: All executed code (Inputs 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7) ran to completion, including the newly added MetFrag section run twice (success and documented-failure case) and the newly TIE_MARGIN-extended library-matching code exercised on a genuine matchms tie. Input 2 (SIRIUS) was not executed due to the same external login gate as the pre-fix audit (TOOLS.md), not an unrunnable-code failure, so it does not trigger this dimension.

functional_suitability.note: The pre-fix gap (MetFrag named as a route with zero executable guidance) is fixed: the new MetFrag section has a full params.txt template and CLI line, verified runnable verbatim in Input 3. Docks 1 point because, unlike its own worked matchms/SIRIUS blocks, the MetFrag section still gives only the params.txt/CSV schema, not a filled-in sample peaklist.txt/candidates.csv -- an agent must still originate real peak masses and candidate chemistry from outside knowledge to run it, just a narrower gap than before.

reliability.note: The Common Errors table and Version Compatibility note are now factually correct for matchms 0.33+ (AssertionError, not silent zero score) -- verified by direct execution in Input 1. Docks 1 point: the inline code comment on the `add_precursor_mz(spectrum)` line ('still raises AssertionError here') is placed on the filter call itself, but the assertion actually fires later, inside ModifiedCosine.pair()/calculate_scores at scoring time -- confirmed by isolating the two calls in Input 1's script. The prose Version Compatibility paragraph gets this right ('raises ... afterward'); the code comment's 'here' could mislead an agent into expecting the crash one line earlier than it occurs.

performance_context.note: Still a single ~250-line SKILL.md, usage-guide.md, and one example script; the new MetFrag section adds ~25 lines without bloating the document.

agent_usability.note: Decision-tree table and Per-Method Failure Modes section remain a cold-start-usable, consistently-labeled workflow; the new MetFrag section follows the same goal/approach/code/gotcha structure as the matchms and SIRIUS sections, so the format stays consistent.

human_usability.note: The pre-fix gap (no documented recovery path for MetFrag) is fixed: the CSV-quoting gotcha and 'check row count, not exit code' warning give an agent a real recovery path, verified accurate by reproducing the exact silent-drop failure in Input 3.

security.note: Unchanged: SIRIUS login uses an env-var pattern, never a hardcoded credential; no injection vectors in any code pattern, including the new MetFrag params.txt block.

maintainability.note: The pre-fix gap (shipped example had no self-check) is fixed: examples/annotate_features.py now asserts its own two expected levels and was confirmed to exit 0 with both asserts passing in Input 7 -- a real regression guard against a future matchms bump, addressing the prior Testability gap.

agent_specific.note: Unchanged: precise trigger description, correct progressive disclosure, bidirectional Related-Skills cross-references, fully deterministic logic (re-confirmed across all 6 executed inputs), explicit escape hatches.

key_strengths: All three P1 findings from the pre-fix audit are fixed and independently re-verified by direct execution, not just inspection: the precursor_mz AssertionError regression (Input 1), the MetFrag section now runs verbatim from SKILL.md end to end including its own documented CSV-quoting failure mode (Input 3), and the matchms tie-detection logic now correctly catches a genuine isomer tie it previously could not (Input 5).

The fix did not introduce a false-positive tie: a new adversarial test (Input 6) confirms the TIE_MARGIN logic leaves a genuine single-best match alone rather than over-flagging structurally similar-but-distinct library entries.
Both P2 fixes to the shipped example (corrected docstring, added self-check asserts) hold up under an unmodified run of the actual shipped file (Input 7), not a re-derived copy.
The MSI/Schymanski confidence-level framing, reference sourcing, and pathway-safety flagging logic remain rigorous and unchanged from the pre-fix audit's strengths.

recommendations.title: Inline code comment misplaces where the precursor_mz AssertionError actually fires
recommendations.problem: The comment on `spectrum = add_precursor_mz(spectrum)` says 'a spectrum with no derivable precursor_mz still raises AssertionError here' -- but add_precursor_mz() itself only logs a warning; the AssertionError actually fires later, inside ModifiedCosine.pair() at calculate_scores() time. Verified by isolating the two calls: add_precursor_mz() completes with a warning, the crash happens on the next call.
recommendations.root_cause: The comment was written to summarize the Version Compatibility paragraph's correct 'raises ... afterward' wording but compressed it onto the filter line itself, losing the 'afterward'.
recommendations.fix: Move the AssertionError comment to the calculate_scores()/ModifiedCosine() line, or reword to 'a spectrum with no derivable precursor_mz will raise AssertionError when scored below, not here'.

recommendations.title: MetFrag section gives the params.txt template and CSV schema but no worked sample data
recommendations.problem: Unlike the matchms section (full runnable synthetic example in examples/annotate_features.py) and SIRIUS's complete bash chain, the new MetFrag section supplies only the params.txt key/value template and the candidates.csv column schema -- an agent must still originate real peak masses and a real candidate structure list from outside knowledge to actually run it, as this audit did.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix prioritized closing the 'zero executable guidance' P1 gap with a runnable template; a fully worked data sample was out of scope for that fix.
recommendations.fix: Ship a small worked candidates.csv + peaklist.txt (e.g. the citrate/isocitrate/glucose triple this Skill's own prose already describes) alongside examples/annotate_features.py so an agent can run the MetFrag path with zero external chemistry lookup, mirroring the matchms example's self-containedness.
